notes.summary: Correlation measures how strongly two variables move together; regression gives the line used to predict one from the other. JSO asks on Karl Pearson's r, Spearman's rank correlation, regression coefficients and finding means and r from two regression lines.

concepts.title: Karl Pearson's correlation
concepts.body:
• r = Cov(x, y)/(σxσy); −1 ≤ r ≤ 1.
  • r = +1 perfect positive, −1 perfect negative, 0 no linear relation.
  • r is unaffected by change of origin and scale (sign flips if exactly one scale factor is negative).
  • A scatter diagram shows the direction and strength visually.

concepts.title: Spearman's rank correlation
concepts.body: R = 1 − 6Σd²/(n(n² − 1)), where d = difference in ranks. Used for qualitative data (beauty, honesty) or ranks. For tied ranks, add the correction m(m² − 1)/12 to Σd² for each tie.

concepts.title: Regression
concepts.body:
• Line of y on x: y − ȳ = byx(x − x̄), byx = r σy/σx.
  • Line of x on y: x − x̄ = bxy(y − ȳ), bxy = r σx/σy.
  • r = ±√(byx × bxy), same sign as the coefficients. Their product cannot exceed 1.
  • Both lines pass through (x̄, ȳ), so the means are found by solving them together.

varieties.name: Karl Pearson's r
varieties.how: Use r = Cov/(σxσy) and remember the range and properties.

example.q: Cov(x, y) = 12, σx = 3, σy = 5. Find r.

varieties.name: Spearman's rank correlation
varieties.how: Find d for each pair, square and add, then use 1 − 6Σd²/(n(n² − 1)).

varieties.name: Regression coefficients and lines
varieties.how: Solve the two lines for the means; to find r, decide which line is y on x so that b_yx × b_xy ≤ 1.

tips: r is the geometric mean of the two regression coefficients.
If r = ±1 the two regression lines coincide; if r = 0 they are perpendicular.
Check your guess of which line is y on x: if b_yx × b_xy > 1, swap.
traps: r = 0 does not mean "no relation", only no linear relation.
Both regression coefficients and r always have the same sign.
In Spearman's formula the denominator is n(n² − 1), not n² − 1.

formulas.name: Regression coefficients
formulas.expr: byx = r σy/σx,  bxy = r σx/σy

questions.q: Karl Pearson's coefficient of correlation always lies between:
questions.solution: −1 ≤ r ≤ +1. r = +1 is perfect positive and r = −1 perfect negative correlation.

questions.q: The two regression coefficients are b<sub>xy</sub> = 0.8 and b<sub>yx</sub> = 0.2. The correlation coefficient r is:
questions.solution: r = √(b<sub>xy</sub> × b<sub>yx</sub>) = √(0.8 × 0.2) = √0.16 = 0.4. Positive, because both coefficients are positive.

questions.q: For 5 pairs of ranks, Σd² = 10. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is:
r = 0.6, σ<sub>x</sub> = 4 and σ<sub>y</sub> = 8. The regression coefficient of y on x is:
The two regression lines are 3x + 2y = 26 and 6x + y = 31. The means x̄ and ȳ are:
questions.solution:
Both lines pass through (x̄, ȳ). From the second: y = 31 − 6x.
Put in the first: 3x + 2(31 − 6x) = 26 ⇒ 3x + 62 − 12x = 26 ⇒ −9x = −36 ⇒ x = 4.
y = 31 − 24 = 7. So x̄ = 4, ȳ = 7.

questions.q: For the regression lines 3x + 2y = 26 and 6x + y = 31, the correlation coefficient r is:
questions.solution:
Try 3x + 2y = 26 as y on x: y = 13 − 1.5x, so byx = −1.5.
Then 6x + y = 31 as x on y: x = 31/6 − y/6, so bxy = −1/6.
Product = 1.5/6 = 0.25 ≤ 1, so this choice is valid (the other choice gives product 4 > 1).
r = −√0.25 = −0.5 (negative, same sign as the coefficients).

flashcards.back: ±√(byx · bxy), sign same as the coefficients
